methodology.title: Know what is behind the insight.
methodology.subtitle: Good decisions need transparency. Here are the sources, assumptions, and things this demo cannot tell you.
methodology.formulaNote: Backend formula integration point—not a validated agronomic model.
methodology.independent: FIELDWISE is an independent NASA Space Apps 2026 project concept. It is not endorsed by NASA.
methodology.imageryNote: The welcome landscape is AI-generated, illustrative, and replaceable. It is not a photograph of the demo farm. Maps use public OpenStreetMap/CARTO basemaps.
methodology.privacyNote: Farm setup and checklist progress stay in your browser's local storage in demo mode. Location permission is optional. Map providers receive standard map tile requests.
methodology.date: Documentation examples, not live dataset verification.

limitations.regional: A regional pixel can contain many farms. It cannot resolve conditions in this individual field.
limitations.clouds: Cloud cover leaves gaps in the illustrative optical time series.
limitations.unavailable: No usable ECOSTRESS observation is included in this demo.
limitations.terrain: This height grid is synthetic. It is not surveyed elevation and cannot support engineering decisions.
limitations.surface: Satellite soil moisture represents near-surface conditions, not the full crop root zone.
limitations.noSoilTest: No laboratory soil test is available.
limitations.notForecast: Historical patterns are not forecasts of the next growing season.
limitations.scale: Resampling a coarse dataset does not create finer measurement accuracy.
limitations.simulated: Every numeric value in this demonstration is simulated. No live satellite retrieval is performed.
limitations.dates: The selected dates do not contain a complete time series.
limitations.regionalTerrain: Elevation source resolution does not imply surveyed boundary accuracy.

evidence.water: The demo rotation gives lower water-demand crops a higher illustrative water-saving score.
evidence.soil: Legume and cover-crop diversity receives a higher soil-health score in this example.
evidence.climate: A more diverse sequence is given a higher illustrative resilience score.
evidence.profit: Illustrative input-cost assumptions favor low-input crops; no local prices were retrieved.
evidence.erosion: Longer periods of ground cover receive a higher illustrative erosion-protection score.
evidence.diversity: The demo counts crop-family diversity within the proposed sequence.

assumptions.water: The example assumes drip irrigation can be maintained.
assumptions.soil: The example assumes residues can remain on the field.
assumptions.climate: The comparison assumes the same farm area for all strategies.
assumptions.profit: Labor and crop prices are fixed demonstration assumptions.
assumptions.erosion: The example assumes cover is maintained during the rainy season.
assumptions.diversity: The example assumes seed for the alternative crops is locally available.

risks.water: Actual irrigation needs depend on crop stage, weather, and soil. Do not set watering rates from this demo.
risks.soil: Cover crops may compete for water in a dry season. Get local advice before changing practice.
risks.market: Alternative crops may have different buyers, labor needs, and market risks.

mock.recommendation: Use the water-conservation example as a conversation starter with a local agricultural adviser, not as a final prescription.

method.weightedBody: Total = Σ(score × weight) ÷ Σ(weight), excluding criteria with no confidence. Scores run from 0 to 100; weights run from 1 to 5. Missing scores are not treated as zero.
method.areaBody: Turf calculates geodesic polygon area on the client. Hectares = m² ÷ 10,000. Dunam = m² ÷ 1,000. This is not a cadastral survey.
method.terrainBody: The viewer builds a surface mesh from the API height grid. Displayed layer colors and both dates are synthetic. Vertical exaggeration affects appearance, not reported elevation.
method.futureBody: Replace this section with the validated calculation definitions, calibration, uncertainty, and version identifiers supplied by your backend.
